numerical_failure.observed_behavior: Negating the point at infinity O (EllipticCurvePoint.point_at_infinity(E)) returns a non-canonical infinity point with coordinates (0, -1, 0) instead of (0, 1, 0), so the assertion comparing (neg_O.x, neg_O.y, neg_O.z) with (O.x, O.y, O.z) fails with AssertionError.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: -O should return the canonical infinity point (0, 1, 0), i.e. the same coordinates as O.
trigger_conditions: Negating the point at infinity, i.e. an EllipticCurvePoint with z == 0
Reproducer uses E = EllipticCurve(0, 0) and O = EllipticCurvePoint.point_at_infinity(E), then neg_O = -O
oracle_clues: assert (neg_O.x, neg_O.y, neg_O.z) == (O.x, O.y, O.z) raises AssertionError on the buggy revision
Fix adds a check: if self.z == 0 return self.point_at_infinity(self._curve)
Regression test added to existing test_elliptic_curve function

category_specific_evidence: Negating the point at infinity (z == 0) previously produced (0, -1, 0) instead of the canonical infinity point (0, 1, 0), per PR#28567 release note.
Reproducer from issue#28546: E = EllipticCurve(0, 0); O = EllipticCurvePoint.point_at_infinity(E); neg_O = -O; assert (neg_O.x, neg_O.y, neg_O.z) == (O.x, O.y, O.z) fails with AssertionError.
Fix adds an early check in __neg__: if self.z == 0, return self.point_at_infinity(self._curve), otherwise the original negation formula -y - a1*x - a3 is used.
The violated property is that the negation of the point at infinity should yield the canonical infinity representation (0, 1, 0) with identical coordinates to O.
reproduction_risks: Passages do not state the exact numerical values of the failing neg_O tuple beyond the (0, -1, 0) versus (0, 1, 0) contrast in the release note.
The fix's test file change only adds an import of EllipticCurvePoint; no explicit test body for the negation case is shown in the passages.
